name: CockroachDB
summary: A distributed SQL database that maps relational requests to replicated key-value ranges, coordinates transactions with MVCC and hybrid-logical timestamps, and commits range writes through Raft quorums.

features.name: Layered SQL to range execution
features.description: CockroachDB translates SQL requests into key-value operations, distributes the keyspace into contiguous ranges, and presents replicated ranges as a single distributed SQL database.
benefits: Provides a PostgreSQL-compatible relational interface over distributed storage
Allows requests to enter through any node while range routing hides data placement
costs: Cross-layer routing and range metadata add coordination paths
Data distribution and range splits affect transaction and query locality

features.name: Raft-replicated ranges and leases
features.description: Each range is replicated as a Raft group; a leaseholder/Raft leader coordinates requests and a quorum of replicas must agree before a write is committed.
benefits: Maintains a consistent replicated range state across node failures
Supports automatic replica repair and rebalancing
costs: Quorum loss stops writes that require consensus
Replication and leadership changes add network and storage latency

features.name: Distributed MVCC transactions
features.description: CockroachDB coordinates transactions spanning ranges with MVCC values, write intents, transaction records, and hybrid-logical-clock timestamps; SERIALIZABLE is the default isolation level.
benefits: Provides atomic multi-range changes and serializable ordering
Supports globally consistent snapshots and historical follower reads
costs: Contention can force transaction retries and client handling
Clock bounds, intent resolution, and transaction records add operational complexity

mathematical_views.question: How does a distributed SQL keyspace refine into contiguous ranges whose Raft-committed transitions preserve a single logical database state?
assumptions: Each range has a well-defined key interval and Raft commit order
A quorum commit is the authoritative transition for the range
The view abstracts SQL planning and physical storage layout

mathematical_views.question: Under what conditions do hybrid-logical timestamps, write intents, and transaction records establish an atomic serializable history across ranges?
assumptions: MVCC versions are ordered by transaction timestamps
Intent and transaction-record states are resolved according to the documented protocol
Clock-offset and retry rules are treated as explicit system assumptions

benefits: Relational semantics over elastic distributed key-value placement
costs: Routing, splitting, and cross-range execution add coordination overhead
Availability and write latency depend on replica quorum health
Retries, intents, timestamps, and contention complicate application behavior
